_about: Every numbered line of BLUEPRINT.md section 2 (house law since 2026-10-05; version 1.1 of 2026-10-06), keyed by its line number. `text` and `number` are that line's two cells, quoted exactly. `need` = the line's numbers as the code reads them (shares as fractions), `op` = how a value is held against `need` ("above" / "more than" = >, "or more" = >=, "at most" / "or less" = <=). `also` = a number that comes from a reading of the line, not from its words; `note` says which. A change here is a change of the law: it needs the owner's word. Locked by tests/test_blueprint_rules.py.

0.1.text: The reason, in one sentence: why it should make money and who is on the losing side

0.2.text: The rule: one entry trigger, at most 2 filters, exits from the standard table only

0.3.text: Its home: market, session and bar size (or "all" when the reason does not single one out)

0.4.text: Where else it should work (its neighbors). A place it should NOT work is no longer asked for (owner, 2026-10-07: "remove the test when it should not"): a card that names one still has it run and shown, no line reads it

0.5.text: The main setting and its 3-4 values

0.6.text: Whether it trades both sides or one side only, and why

0.7.text: When it should lose: one stretch or kind of market in which the idea must lose money. A build without that loss is a red flag, and no filter is added only to erase it
0.7.note: owner 2026-10-06, the course's extra lesson (the drawdown is the premium). The card says it in words; nobody can check a filter's motive by machine: the round's reason (2.9) is read against it by the owner

1.1.text: Every trade is entered inside the stated session window

1.2.text: One position at a time, and every trade is flat by 15:58 ET (13:13 on half days)
1.2.note: flat by 15:58 = closed before 15:59:00: the engine flattens on the first print at or after 15:58:00 (the reading of run_menus.hold_checks); a half day = the engine's calendar (l2sim.EARLY_CLOSES, equity-index markets only; gold keeps 15:58)

1.3.text: The number of trades is what the rule implies (for example, never more than the stated maximum per day)

1.4.text: With a stop and a target on, winners pay about the target and losers cost about the stop, in dollars; exceptions are listed

1.5.text: 10 trades are looked at on the chart (the first 5 and 5 at random): entry and exit sit where the rule says. *(10 is my number; the course gives none)*
1.5.note: the 5 at random are drawn with this fixed seed from the trades after the first 5, so the same trade list always shows the same 10 (blueprint/checks.py)

1.6.text: After any change to the code, the earlier trade list is reproduced exactly before a new run counts

2.1.note: profitable = above $0, for a variant and for the average variant: the judge's test (1) and the dry run of section 3 (funnel.py) also ask the average variant to be profitable

2.2.text: The average trade is big enough (net of all variants ÷ their trades)
2.2.note: dollars per trade after costs, 1 contract; gold = GC

2.3.text: It beats random entries with the same stops and targets
2.3.number: above 95 % of random tables in round 1; 97.5 %, 98.3 %, 98.75 %, 99 % in rounds 2, 3, 4, 5
2.3.note: by round; "above" is strict (toolkit_plan.md section 6, decision 3); the random tables are control.json

2.4.note: a dry run on fewer months than the build also shows "on pace" = need x its months / the build's months

2.5.text: Its neighbors agree: the same idea on the next bar sizes and in the other sessions it should fit
2.5.number: half or more of those tables profitable

2.6.text: Long and short each make money on their own (an idea that is one-sided by its card is judged on that side)
2.6.note: all variants together; a table with trades on one side only is judged on that side

2.7.text: A filter is kept only if it wins alone: the plain version plus that one filter beats the plain version
2.7.number: higher average trade, and that round's random bar
2.7.note: higher average trade than the plain version AND line 2.3 at that round's bar

2.8.text: Monte Carlo: it still meets 2.1 and 2.2 in most reshuffled runs

2.9.number: at most 5, each with its reason written before the run

3.1.text: Saved: the rule, the variant list, the default variant (the middle survivor, never the best), the control and the costs
3.1.note: the default = the middle of the variants profitable on build and on build with worse fills (toolkit_plan.md section 6, decision 3)

3.2.text: From here nothing changes. A change is a new version: back to phase 2, and its earlier unseen read is marked as used

3.3.text: The default variant has a healthy profit factor (its winning trades ÷ its losing trades, in dollars)
3.3.note: lines 3.3-3.7: the default variant of 3.1 alone, on the build days, after costs at 1 contract (owner 2026-10-06; the course reads its numbers on the one setting it trades). No losing trade = met; no trade = not met

3.4.text: Its profit is large against its worst drawdown (its net ÷ its worst drawdown, open losses counted)
3.4.note: the drawdown counts OPEN LOSSES (owner 2026-10-07: the course is read for a prop account, and the firm's drawdown is breached by an open loss): the largest fall from the high of the end-of-day running total to the lowest point reached, a day's close or its worst open point (where the day started minus the day's worst open loss: each trade's MAE and commission), on every session day of the build range. The bar is the course's first screen (return on max drawdown above 3); this line read closed days until 2026-10-07, and with open losses the same strategy reads lower. No drawdown at all and a profit = met

3.5.text: Its Sharpe is high enough (its result on every session day, per year) *(the owner's line; the course has none)*
3.5.note: mean ÷ standard deviation of the net of every session day of the build range (a day without a trade = 0), times the square root of 252

3.6.text: Its worst drawdown fits the account at the smallest size: at 1 micro, open losses counted, it stays under the drawdown limit of LucidPro 50K
3.6.note: the worst drawdown of 3.4 (open losses counted) ÷ the micros of a contract (sizes.json), strictly under the account's trailing limit: at the limit the account is bust. The owner's account of 2026-10-06 (the course, lesson 10: a strategy must fit the account at one micro). `rule_file` = that account in the app's prop simulator: the lock SHOWS the default variant's prop odds on the build days for it (owner 2026-10-07; a number on the card, never a pass line)

3.7.text: Monte Carlo on the default variant alone: it makes money in almost all reshuffled runs of the build days
3.7.number: 90 % of the runs or more (the course's line)
3.7.note: the runs of montecarlo.json (the same draws as line 2.8) on the default variant's own days

4.1.text: Both parts make money on their own: Jul-Dec 2025 and Jan-Sep 2026
4.1.note: the two parts are ranges.json test.parts

4.2.text: The whole test: the average and the middle variant make money
4.2.note: middle variant = the median (toolkit_plan.md section 6, decision 3)

4.3.text: The average trade is still big enough

4.5.text: It still makes money with worse fills
4.5.number: 2 ticks + 250 ms (+ 100 ms late cancel for two-sided brackets)
4.5.note: makes money = the average variant above $0 with these fills (costs.json worse)

4.6.text: It still makes money without its 3 best days
4.6.note: read on the average variant (toolkit_plan.md section 6, decision 3)

4.7.text: Monte Carlo: it makes money in almost all reshuffled runs of the test period
4.7.number: 90 % of the runs or more (the course's line)
4.7.note: makes money = the average variant above $0 in a run; the runs are montecarlo.json

4.8.text: The test looks like the build: the average trade (the reading of 4.3) holds against the build's own average trade of line 2.2
4.8.number: at least half of the build's
4.8.note: the build's average trade = line 2.2 of the frozen table (the lock's variants on the build days), kept in the lock. "half" is the toolkit author's number; the course says the two should look alike and gives none

4.9.text: The default variant still has a healthy profit factor on the test days
4.9.note: line 3.3's reading on the test days

5.1.text: Both phases are run: passing the eval, and getting paid on the funded account, each at its own best size from the pre-set size steps

5.2.text: Both are read on a "live is worse" row, not on the plain backtest
5.2.number: win rate -5 points and winners -15 % *(the course's middle case; my pick)*

5.3.text: Portfolio: the odds are good enough to buy
5.3.number: The owner's bar of 2026-10-03, until he changes it: eval pass within 10 trading days 60 % or more; maximum payout within 20 trading days 75 % or more
5.3.note: the PORTFOLIO's bar since version 1.1 (bp.py portfolio); bp.py sim says how one strategy reads on it and does not judge it. The owner's numbers of 2026-10-03

5.4.text: Written on the eval card before the first eval: how many attempts, and the total fee budget
5.4.number: set by the owner for each strategy

5.5.text: One strategy: it is more likely to pass its eval than to bust it, and more likely to be paid than to bust the funded account *(my numbers)*
5.5.number: eval: a pass before a bust 50 % or more; funded: a first payout before a bust 50 % or more
5.5.note: bp.py sim: ONE strategy at each phase's best size, on the "live is worse" row. No day limit: a walk goes on for the app's own horizon (propsim.HORIZON = 250 trading days, or the account's maximum days); a path still open then is neither. The numbers are the toolkit author's (the owner: "yeah i like it"); a strategy with no edge passes a $3,000 target against a $2,000 drawdown about 4 times in 10

5.6.text: Portfolio: every strategy in it has passed the out-of-sample test on its own, and no two of them are the same idea on the same market
5.6.note: bp.py portfolio. A member that is not proven on history has no test-period trades and is refused. The same idea on the same market = the same entry trigger there, or default variants that take the same side on judge.SAME_SIDE or more of judge.SAME_DAYS or more shared build days

5.7.text: Portfolio: a strategy is added only when it raises the portfolio's eval odds; one that lowers them stays out
5.7.note: bp.py portfolio: the portfolio's eval odds (line 5.3's, within its days, at its best size) against the same without that member -- the others alone, at their own best size of the whole account. Raises = strictly higher

6.1.text: Live equals the test, every day of the eval: each live trade matches the tester's replay of that day. A mismatch is a bug: it is fixed before the count goes on
6.1.number: same entry time, same exit reason
6.1.note: "same entry time" = the live entry fill within 5 seconds of the replay's entry: room for latency and for the clocks of two machines, and far inside the smallest bar (60 s), so an entry on another bar is a mismatch (blueprint/evalcard.py; a reading, easy to change). "same exit reason" = the same of target, stop and clock (the engine's time / eod and the desk's flat are one reason); any other reason is compared as it is written

6.2.text: Stage A, the first days at 1 micro: fills are close to the test
6.2.number: average entry slip 2 ticks or less; no missed or rejected order

6.3.text: Stage A is passed after 5 clean trades *(my number)*; then the size goes to the simulator's size

6.4.text: Stage B, at size, read after 10, 20, 30 and 40 trades: drawdown against the Monte Carlo table of its own history
6.4.number: under the 75th percentile: carry on · at the 75th: cut size · at the 95th: the hard alarm (line 6.9)

6.5.text: Stage B: after 40 trades the average trade holds up
6.5.number: at least half of history; otherwise the soft alarm (line 6.6)

6.6.text: The soft alarm is a review, not a switch-off by itself: has this happened in the test history, can it be explained, is it inside normal behaviour
6.6.number: three yes: carry on · otherwise: stop until it recovers (line 6.9)

6.7.text: During the eval only the size may change, never the rule

6.8.text: A bust inside the drawdown table does not retire the strategy; running out of the attempts in 5.4 does

6.9.text: The hard alarm: the strategy is switched off, and no review turns it back on. A stop is not a deletion: it comes back when the tester's replay of the days since shows it has recovered
6.9.number: last 5 months positive · last 12 months positive · last 3 months above its long-run pace
6.9.note: the course, lesson 3 (owner 2026-10-06: "lets use his rule"). Read by the eval card when the tester's replay since the stop is sent with the fills (replay_since_stop): calendar months back from the replay's last day, a micro, on the variant's test-period trades and the replay; the long-run pace = the whole record a month. Not sent: a rule to follow
